name: martial-arts-body-discipline
description: Martial arts as body discipline — the shared pedagogical structure across striking, grappling, and weapon arts (stance, distance, timing, ukemi, live partner work, graded ranking, and the ethical container the best schools enforce). Covers karate, judo, jiu-jitsu (Brazilian and traditional Japanese), aikido, kendo/kenjutsu, boxing, muay Thai, and wrestling at enough depth that an agent can place a user into a reasonable first-month practice and recognize the safety failures that matter most. Leans on Moshé Feldenkrais's judo background and Yang Jwing-Ming's martial scholarship for the internal-to-external bridge. Use for any query about beginning a martial art, training injury patterns, graded progression, or the ethics of combat training.
